title: Longitude and Latitude: The Earth as a Sphere
seo_title: Longitude and Latitude – SSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find differences in latitude and longitude; find distances along meridians and parallels of latitude; find the radius of a parallel; solve time and longitude problems. (summary of the NERDC SSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 maths worksheets on longitude and latitude: difference in longitude, distances along a meridian and a parallel of latitude, radius of a parallel and local time. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Along a parallel: θ/360 × 2πR cos α
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Lines of latitude run east–west; lines of longitude (meridians) run north–south.
  • On the same meridian, distance = (difference in latitude)/360 × 2πR.
  • On a parallel of latitude α, the radius is R cos α, so distance = θ/360 × 2πR cos α.

Examples

Example

15°E and 45°W

One E, one W: add

Answer: Difference 60°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Subtracting when one is east and one is westAdd them.
Using R on a parallelUse R cos α.
Moving the clock the wrong wayEast is ahead; west is behind.

items.q: Town X is at (2°N, 5°E) and town Y is at (40°S, 5°E). Find the distance XY along the meridian. (Take R = 6,400 km and π = 22/7.)
items.e: The angle at the centre is 42°. Distance = 42/360 × 2πR = 42/360 × 2 × 22/7 × 6,400 ≈ 4,693 km.

items.q: Town Q is 135° west of town P. When it is 11:00 a.m. at P, what is the local time at Q? (The time changes by 1 hour for every 15°.)
